record_identity.title: AI-managed malware and phishing drove Russian-linked espionage operations

incident_identity.date_basis: The 10 September 2026 source identifies the activity but does not give an exact start or end date for this independently bounded workstream; the report's broader December 2025–August 2026 coverage is not imputed as event dates.

summary: Anthropic reports that a Russian-speaking actor operated a human-directed Claude-assisted espionage toolkit that autonomously adapted malware following security detections, supported phishing infrastructure and executed portions of intrusions. The provider attributes distinct successful operations to drone suppliers, compromised hotel Wi-Fi providers, messaging-account victims, a North African government technology authority and cloud-mailbox organisations. The actor obtained credentials and confidential data, but complete model-to-target execution paths are not public. Microsoft separately documented related CaptiveCrunch hospitality attacks and AI support; overlap does not independently verify every Anthropic-reported AI action.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Anthropic attributes a coordinated Russian-speaking espionage campaign to human target selection combined with AI-managed malware refactoring, phishing infrastructure, intrusion commands and data theft. Several real victim compromises are reported, but no complete per-victim sequence of model actions is public. Microsoft Threat Intelligence independently documented overlapping CaptiveCrunch hospitality-network compromises and AI-assisted activity, with partly distinct actor designators. Anthropic separately reports theft of drone software and mailboxes, guest traffic redirection at three hospitality vendors, WhatsApp message exports, more than 300,000 national identity records at a North African authority, and mail access at eight organisations. These remain distinct source-attributed victim pathways; total record counts are not treated as unique injured people.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Victims are not pooled into one severity claim; the operation is distinct from the previously recorded 2025 campaign.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The source demonstrates why model-mediated action must be attributed to its particular actor, runtime, authority boundary and material outcome, without imputing human operator decisions to the model.
assessment_boundaries: Victims are not pooled into one severity claim; the operation is distinct from the previously recorded 2025 campaign.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: NIST AC-3 addresses enforcement of approved logical access authorisations over protected systems and information. Anthropic reports that the actor obtained non-public mail, drone-industrial and identity information through compromised victim accounts and environments. These realised unauthorised acquisitions are contrary to access enforcement for the reported operations; this comparison does not claim that every targeted organisation was compromised.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: Direct reviewed information-access class relationship to NIST access enforcement.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: NIST IA-5(g) concerns protection of authenticator secret content. The reported campaign obtained genuine credentials from victim systems and used compromised authentication material in subsequent access, demonstrating a bounded custody failure distinct from the broader data acquisition. The report does not show that all scanned or targeted accounts had their authenticators disclosed.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: Direct reviewed secret-custody class relationship to NIST authenticator protection.
